causal_disconnection: Steering cells k=0 (ballot, Delta_i(1)) and k=1 (Delta_i'(1)) of row i modifies sigma_i only at coefficients x^{d_i-1}, x^{d_i}; the perturbation descends exactly 1 coefficient per row (division by x) and can first touch the die-deciding constant coefficient at row >= i + d_i - k - 1 >= d_0 - 2 ~ gamma* R. All observed transient dies are at rows 61..121 << gamma* R, hence provably invariant under ANY schedule of the top cells. Confirmed bit-identical empirically: R=256 D0=0, policies none/zero/tent/tent+k1 all die at row 61, const 2^139, identical head bits and junk bits every row, while sigma(1)-trajectories differ wildly (5 vs -1 vs 61-on-target). die_anatomy: Two-phase. Closure mode (R=128 D0=0, R=256 D0=1): head coefficients stay EXACTLY +-1 (E-form) for the whole run -- peak headbits=1; the giant q^{R-1} binomial mass (2^251 at R=256) sits in a mid band above the head and is chewed down by the clamp; per-row clamp junk decays monotonically to 0 (2^243 at row 0 -> 0). Die mode (R=256 D0=0, R=512 D0<=4): junk injection decays only to ~2^180 by row ~30 then re-grows; the mid-band wavefront descends into the head (headbits jump 1 -> 157 at row 56 of 61, growth ~8.6 bits/row) and the constant overflows ~5 rows later. The +-1 forced-cell schedule never enters the mechanism.
ballot_trajectory_of_closures: In verified closures rule A's sigma_i(1) does NOT ride the tent early: it dithers near 0 during the transient, then climbs at +1/row, locking onto the tent's descending branch R-3-i from row ~0.63R (row 81 of 128; row 159 of 256) to the end. Max deviation from tent ~ R/4 at midrun. The ballot cut (S4) is slack in the greedy family's transient window; it binds only in the locked tail.
interpretation: Rule A's transient die is a bulk-capacity failure of the cellwise clamp in the HIGH cells k ~ d (low coefficients): the truncated ideal's cells exceed Lucas caps by hundreds of bits and the leftover avalanches. Fixing it requires changing the bulk clamp / ideal target (or paying D0), not the ballot cells. Ballot scheduling remains free and harmless (and tent+k1 is attractor-compatible), so it can be composed with any bulk fix for endgame control, but it is NOT the transient cure. Search negatives are not infeasibility evidence: the profile itself may still close at lower D0 via LP/beam.
